archetype.name: Playoff Team (goalie-backed, deep down the middle)
archetype.definition: A Boston side that wins on 5-on-5 chance quality, a long rotation of centers and an in-form Jeremy Swayman, with special teams lagging behind the rest of the game.

report.headline: A real margin under the record, inflated for now by Swayman and finishing
report.take:
Seven games in, Boston is 5-2-0 and sits fifth on the site. The record is not the interesting part. Most teams this early are living on one-goal games, and the Bruins are not. They have outscored opponents 26-16. Their Pts vs Goal Diff is slightly negative at -0.9, so if anything the standings undersell them. Both losses were flat 1-4 nights against Minnesota and Ottawa. The wins include 6-1, 5-1 and 6-3 routs in the last three games.

The engine is a mix of goaltending and depth. Swayman has started six of seven, sits second on the goalie tab and owns a .930 Save % and 4.9 GSAx. That lands the team top-ten in Goalies GSAx and third in goals against. Up front there is no single carrier. Pastrnak leads with 8 points on 27 shots, but Fraser Minten has 4 goals and seven different forwards have two. The lineup is stacked with centers, and nearly every one of them is above 50% in xGF %. That is why the forward grade is an A- without a superstar points pace beyond Pastrnak.

What the numbers hide is a PDO of 107.6. That is far above the 100 baseline, and some of the gap between the shot share and the scoreboard will fade. The 5-on-5 picture is solid but not dominant: a 54.2 xGF % ranks tenth, and a 49% CF % ranks 18th. Boston is generating better chances than it allows without owning the puck. The special teams are a genuine weak spot. The power play converts at 16.7% and the penalty kill at 76%, both bottom-half. That PK figure sits close to last season's 77%.

History supports the shape. Last season's 45-27-10 team was carried by 30.6 goalie GSAx with a sub-48 xGF %. This version's chance share is meaningfully better, which makes the start more believable than last year's. Expect the goals per game to cool as the PDO normalizes. A team with this depth, this goalie and a positive expected-goals share is a playoff team even after the regression.

strengths.title: Swayman in top form
strengths.body: Swayman ranks second of 64 goalies, with a .930 Save % and nearly five goals saved above expected in six starts. Last season he and the staff produced 30.6 GSAx, so this is not a fluke profile. Expect the save percentage to drift down from .930, but elite-adjacent goaltending is a reasonable baseline.

strengths.title: Scoring by committee down the middle
strengths.body: Nine forwards share the minutes with no one but Pastrnak above 19.5 TOI. Seven forwards have at least two goals, led by Minten's four. Geekie, Lindholm, Mittelstadt and Hagens all sit above 50% in xGF %. Depth like this holds up better than a top-line-only attack, though Minten's finishing rate will likely cool.

strengths.title: Wins built on margin, not luck
strengths.body: Goal Diff / GP ranks fifth in the league. The team is actually slightly under its goal-differential points, the opposite of a lucky start. A 54.2 xGF % means the chance quality backs a good share of that margin, even if the scoreboard runs ahead of it.

concerns.title: PDO far above sustainable
concerns.body: A 107.6 PDO says the shooting and save percentages at 5-on-5 are both running hot. A 49% CF % shows Boston is not controlling possession. When the bounces even out, some of those 6-1 and 5-1 nights become one-goal games. This is the main reason the goals-per-game pace should come down.

concerns.title: Special teams dragging
concerns.body: The PP % and PK % both rank in the bottom half. The penalty kill at 76% matches last season's 77%, which makes it look structural rather than a slow start. The power play is the likelier one to improve, since it converted at 23.4% a year ago.

concerns.title: Little cover behind Swayman
concerns.body: DiPietro's lone start produced a 3.11 GAA and negative GSAx, and he sits 54th of 64 goalies. The A goaltending grade rests almost entirely on one goalie. Any dip or absence from Swayman exposes it quickly.

trend.note: A quick 2-0 start gave way to back-to-back 1-4 losses. Boston answered with three straight wins, each by three goals or more, and that matches its longest streak of the season.

weekAhead.headline: Three road games out West, then Nashville at home
weekAhead.body:
Boston plays at Anaheim, Los Angeles and Dallas, then comes home for Nashville. Only Anaheim carries a winning record, and the Ducks' 47.4 xGF % and 47% CF % say their 4-2-0 start is running ahead of their play. The Kings are 0-3-2 with an F in both goaltending and blueline grades, a 57.9% PK and -8.1 GSAx. That is the softest matchup of the week on paper. Nashville gets out-chanced badly at 5-on-5, with a 42.3 xGF %.

Dallas is the different test. The Stars are first in goals against, have A+ goaltending, and hold centers and defensemen further under expectation than anyone. Boston's center-heavy depth will find scoring hard that night, but the Stars' 30th-ranked offense also limits the risk. Three of four on the road keeps this from being a gimme. Still, the opponents' underlying numbers are mostly weaker than Boston's.

keyMatchups.title: Boston PK vs Anaheim's power play
keyMatchups.body: Anaheim converts 33.3% of its power plays, third in the league, against a Boston kill at 76%. In a matchup where Boston should win at 5-on-5, penalties are the Ducks' clearest path. Discipline in the opener matters.

keyMatchups.title: Boston wingers vs Los Angeles
keyMatchups.body: The Kings allow wingers well above their expected points, ranking 29th. Their goalies are 30th in GSAx and their kill is 31st. Pastrnak and Peterka are set up for a big night, and so is Boston's struggling power play.

keyMatchups.title: Centers into the Dallas wall
keyMatchups.body: Dallas ranks first at holding centers under their expected points, and Boston's depth is built on centers. The Stars' goalies lead them to the No. 1 defense, while their offense ranks 30th. Expect a low-event game that hinges on Swayman matching their goaltending.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Boston keeps winning the 5-on-5 chance battle on the road as its 107.6 PDO starts to come back toward normal.

restOfSeason.body:
The sustainable parts are Swayman, a deep group of two-way centers and a positive expected-goals share. The parts that will regress are the near-four goals a game and the sub-2.3 goals allowed, both inflated by a PDO well above 100. A reasonable path is a team that keeps outscoring opponents, but by a goal-ish margin rather than routs. That looks like a better version of last season's playoff team, because this year's chance share is stronger.

The ceiling depends on special teams. A power play back near last year's level would add real goals. A kill stuck in the mid-70s will keep costing close games. The floor depends on Swayman's health and form, given how little the backup has shown.
swingFactors: Penalty kill climbing out of the bottom third

confidence.note: Seven games, with the PDO far from 100 and blowout wins shaping the margin.
